newsitem.title: USA: OCC's Ludwig urges avoiding premature e-cash rules.
newsitem.headline: OCC's Ludwig urges avoiding premature e-cash rules.

text.p: U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig on Friday said that governments should avoid premature regulation of electronic money.

"We recognize the dangers of involving government too early in such a rapidly evolving area and do not want to chill or unduly influence the market by encumbering it with regulation that may quickly become outmoded, inappropriate or detrimental," he told an electronic money and banking conference. He stressed, however, that the governments should be prepared to take action when it is required.
Ludwig also spoke of the need for the private and public sectors to work together as the technology evolves.

Looking at ways of ensuring that the market for electronic banking and money remains reliable, Ludwig talked of the need for transactions to be enforceable, pointing out that electronic commerce is borderless by its nature.
"It is unclear what laws apply in many transactions, or what courts have jurisdiction to resolve disputes," he noted.

He also said that it was important for consumers to understand the risks involved in using electronic money and that new electronic forms of payments not get in the way of broad consumer access to financial services.
